notes.text: They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 8 of their last 10 games, including the last one. Gage Goncalves takes shifts on two lines, L2 and L4. J.J. Moser is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Crozier and Carlson.

Yanni Gourde is on the injured non-roster list (hip surgery) and has not played this season. Ilya Mikheyev has taken his spot beside Zemgus Girgensons and Pontus Holmberg. That line has had 53% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 109:32 together.
John Carlson is no longer killing penalties: 1% of the team’s shorthanded time in 15 games, down from 47% with his old team last season.

faceoff.text: Anthony Cirelli is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 65% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 26 seconds at a time, against 70 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by Brandon Hagel (20 of 26 changes).

story.head: Kucherov’s favorite opponent
paras: The Lightning won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 in Tampa Bay on Oct 8. The Wild have won three straight, and the Lightning have won two in a row. Two of the league’s best teams meet. Going in, the Lightning are third in the Atlantic (tied for seventh in the NHL) and the Wild first in the Central (second).
The Lightning’s record (.733) is about what their chances are worth. The Wild’s record (.750) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.673), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Wild (3rd) and the Lightning (5th) both have had some of the best goaltending in the league. The Bolts get into a lot of chippy games (4th). They also keep shots away better than almost anyone (3rd), and something has to give when the Wild’s shooting runs into their defense. On the other side, the Wild draw more penalties than they take (2nd), but get pinned in their own end on long shifts (31st). Minnesota has allowed 2.17 goals a game, the fewest in the league. The Wild are likely to get in the way of a lot of the Lightning’s shots.

Nikita Kucherov (4 G / 16 A / 20 P in 15 GP) leads the Lightning in scoring, with seven points in his last five games and a point in seven straight games against Minnesota. Brandon Hagel (8 G / 9 A / 17 P in 15 GP) has a team-high eight goals. Kirill Kaprizov (16 G / 14 A / 30 P in 18 GP) leads the Wild in scoring and is tied for third in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games and five goals in six games against Tampa Bay since 2023-24. Quinn Hughes (6 G / 19 A / 25 P in 18 GP) isn’t far behind, with nine points in his last five games.

Andrei Vasilevskiy (8-3-1 / .886 SV% in 12 GS) is in line to start for Tampa Bay. Jesper Wallstedt (11-2-3 / .922 SV% in 16 GS) has been terrific for Minnesota and will likely start. Vasilevskiy has a .877 save percentage in six starts against the Wild, well under his usual .911. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
